name: Hirevire
description: Async video interview tool — candidates answer your questions on camera; hiring managers review without scheduling. Plans ~$49 / $149 / $249/mo. India-founded, bootstrapped, team 2–5.

mentions.evidence: ~$13.8k MRR, 162 active subscriptions, ~$14.9k L30, ~$267k all-time, ~180 users claimed, founded Dec 2021, India. Last sync Oct 1, 2026.
mentions.indieAngle: Own one step of hiring (async screen, reference checks, offer letters) for a vertical instead of building a full HRIS.

whyItPrints: Screening calls don't scale. Hirevire productizes "watch every applicant" for SMB recruiters — clear ACV, recurring seats, no need to become an ATS.
whyThisMatters:
Hiring teams use Hirevire so the screening call never has to be scheduled. You write the questions once. You send a link, or you add it to the job post. The candidate records the answers on their phone, whenever they have a quiet minute. You watch later, in a batch if you want. One click sends a response to the hiring manager.

What it gets rid of is the calendar dance. Messages back and forth, a cancellation the hour before, time zones that never line up, and notes you can't quite remember once the manager is free. Startups with a small people team use it. So do companies hiring in more than one country, and recruiters or staffing firms pushing through a lot of applicants in a week. Transcripts cover more than 90 languages. The trial lasts seven days and doesn't need a card. McDonald's and Hertz are named among the customers, with a claim of more than 500 companies.

It was founded in India. Two to five people run it, and it's bootstrapped. It stops at the recorded screen. It doesn't try to replace a full applicant-tracking system. You skip the call you used to book.
